title: Groupoïdes de Teichmüller et les S0 Tg,!ν, S0 TG : notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Title (from the image): 'Généralités sur les groupoïdes'. This is a preliminary definition that serves the later construction of central extensions of the Teichmüller groupoids (the 'S0 T' objects of the dossier).

Setting: C and C' are groupoids, f: C -> C' is a morphism (functor), and π is an abelian group, noted as discrete.

Definition. f is a 'π-fibration', equivalently 'f makes C a central extension of C' by π' (left margin), if:
(a) f is surjective on objects and surjective on arrows between given objects, i.e. full and surjective on objects.
(b) The fibres of f are connected. A fibre is the subgroupoid over an object y with arrows mapping to id_y. Each fibre is given the structure of a connected 'π-groupoid': its fundamental group is commutative and is identified with π by a given isomorphism.

Reformulation:
- Since π is abelian, the identifications glue into a homomorphism π -> End(id_C), the centre of the category. So π acts functorially (naturally) on every object of C.
- For each object x there is a short exact sequence 1 -> π -> Aut_C(x) -> Aut_{C'}(f(x)) -> 1, with π central in Aut_C(x).

Claim. Data (1),(2) satisfying (3) and the bijectivity (4) of π0(f): π0(C) -> π0(C') define a π-fibration if and only if f is surjective on objects.

Check of the claim:
- Fullness: take x, x' over y, y' and an arrow g: y -> y'. By (4) there is some h: x -> x'. Then g∘f(h)^{-1} lies in Aut(y') and lifts by the surjectivity in (3). Hence f is full.
- Connected fibres: for x, x' over y, take h: x -> x' and correct f(h) by a lift of f(h)^{-1}. This gives an arrow over id_y.
- Fibre automorphism groups are the kernel π.
So the claim is right.

Example (begun here, continued on p.89). Let U be a connected, locally 1-connected topological group, so π = π1(U,1) is automatically abelian; this is why 'commutatif' is struck out. Let P be a U_T-torsor over a space T. Then Π1(p): Π1(P) -> Π1(T) acquires a π-structure. The next page says this is a π-fibration when the maps π -> π1(P_i, x_i) behave well; if they have a constant kernel N, one gets a π/N-fibration.

Page 89 then restricts to a set E of base points with an action of a subgroup μ -> U, compatible with E -> P. This is the device for building centrally extended Teichmüller groupoids on 'tangential' or rigidified base points, e.g. U = C* or S^1 torsors such as determinant or tangent-frame bundles, with π = Z.

Purpose: to formalize central extensions of Teichmüller/mapping-class groupoids by π1 of a structure group, presumably Z, as groupoid-level objects.
errors: (2) is written End(id_{C'}) in the image/transcription. For π to act on every object of C it should be End(id_C), the centre of C (the action on C' is trivial). Probably a slip.
Minor: in (a), 'surjective on arrows' must be read as surjective on each Hom-set (fullness), not merely on the total set of arrows. The marginal insertion suggests Grothendieck meant this.

With (3) and (4) assumed, strict surjectivity on objects is the only extra condition. Essential surjectivity already follows from (4), so the 'iff' is correct but the condition is a strictness artefact.

ideas.what: Central extension of a groupoid by an abelian group π: a full functor, surjective on objects, whose fibres are connected π-groupoids, with π mapping to the centre End(id_C) and exact sequences 1->π->Aut(x)->Aut(f x)->1
ideas.modern_name: central extension of groupoids / π-banded gerbe over a groupoid (band = π, abelian)
ideas.usually_credited_to: Giraud (Cohomologie non abélienne, 1971) for banded gerbes; Brown, Mackenzie and others for groupoid extensions
ideas.where_published: Closely related to bands/liens in Giraud's work done under Grothendieck; in Pursuing Stacks only in spirit

ideas.what: Characterization: data (π -> centre, exact sequences on automorphism groups, π0-bijectivity) give a central extension iff f is surjective on objects
ideas.modern_name: elementary lemma on central extensions of groupoids

ideas.what: Fundamental groupoid of a torsor P under a connected topological group U, mapping to Π1(T), as a central extension of Π1(T) by π1(U) (or a quotient π1(U)/N)
ideas.modern_name: central extension of the fundamental groupoid induced by a principal bundle (cf. extensions of mapping class groups from S^1/C*-bundles, e.g. determinant or framing)
ideas.usually_credited_to: folklore; in the Teichmüller context Atiyah (2-framings, 1990), Moore–Seiberg (1989), Bakalov–Kirillov (2001)
ideas.where_published: Esquisse d'un programme mentions Teichmüller towers but not this central-extension construction explicitly

missed.claim: In this dossier (from 1978) Grothendieck sets up a general framework of π-central extensions of groupoids, produced from fundamental groupoids of U-torsors. The context indicates its use for centrally extended Teichmüller groupoids. This parallels the later Z-central extensions of mapping-class/Teichmüller groupoids from conformal field theory (framings, central charge) in Moore–Seiberg and Bakalov–Kirillov. Those works are not connected to Grothendieck's Teichmüller tower programme in the literature.
missed.quote: on dit aussi que f fait de C une extension centrale de C' par π
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: It would document that Grothendieck's Teichmüller tower was intended to include centrally extended (framed or determinant) versions. That links the Grothendieck–Teichmüller programme to the projectively flat or modular-functor setting, where GT actions on centrally extended towers are still only partly understood.

deep.surprise_reason: The page itself is a routine definition and lemma on central extensions of groupoids, plus the start of a standard example. Its only interest is the context hint that Grothendieck intended central extensions of Teichmüller groupoids.
transcription_corrections: Title should read 'Généralités sur les groupoïdes', not 'Centralisations[?] sur les groupoïdes'.
In (2) the image seems to read End(id_{C'}), but mathematically it should be End(id_C).
Second line: 'π un groupe abélien (groupe discret)' — the insertion reads 'groupe discret' (or 'discrets').

In the example, 'commutatif' and the first 'loc. 1-connexe' are struck out and rewritten as 'connexe et loc. 1-connexe'; the strike of 'commutatif' reflects that π1 of a topological group is automatically abelian.
